diagram_math_checks.check: Each horizontal row uses the same increasing real coordinate; thick segments and filled endpoints are exactly the closed intervals [1,2], [2,3], [3,4]. These are the supports specified in the Given clause and supplier [L1].

The dotted line meets [1,2] and lies strictly left of [2,3] and [3,4], agreeing with f_1(3/2)=1 and f_n(3/2)=0 for n≥2. It is explicitly an example, not a claim that an arbitrary fixed x occupies this plotted coordinate. Supplier [L1] proof 1.1 establishes eventual vanishing for every fixed real x once n>x+1.

Each interval has length and Lebesgue measure one. Since f_n is an indicator, {|f_n|>1/2}=[n,n+1]; all three measure labels are correct. This is supplier [L1] proof 1.2 and explains why convergence in measure fails, the premise used with [L2] in existing counterexample step 2.1.
No edge encodes a map or unsupported implication: arrows only orient copies of the real line. The rigorous original two-step proof is unchanged and independent of the figure.
